narrative:
On November 25, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,622 cases across 49 judicial rosters and heard 1,018 matters, resulting in an overall hearing rate of 38.8%. This output closely tracks recent performance trends, matching the 39.0% rate recorded on November 24 (1,062 of 2,723 heard) and the 38.4% rate on November 23 (1,118 of 2,912 heard), while remaining below the 45.1% efficiency benchmark achieved on November 20.

Judicial clearance varied across individual court halls. Highlights included Judge Anant Ramanath Hegde (Hall 26), who disposed of 24 out of 30 listed matters (80.0%) in one session, and Judge K. V. Aravind (Hall 34), who cleared 19 of 22 cases (86.4%) in a supplementary roster. Conversely, Hall 13 under Judge Suraj Govindaraj registered no completed hearings across 147 scheduled listings. By hearing stage, conversion was highest for Further Hearing matters at 63.3% (31 of 49 heard) and Orders at 46.7% (392 of 839 heard). Preliminary Hearings converted at 37.1% (158 of 426), whereas Admissions (32.5%) and Final Hearings (27.4%) recorded lower completion ratios.

Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the single largest share of the workload with 1,110 listings, recording a 34.4% hearing rate (382 cases heard). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) followed with 465 listings and a 33.5% conversion rate (156 cases heard). Higher clearance efficiency was achieved in appellate and revision categories: Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw 50.9% heard (198 of 389), Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reached 56.3% (98 of 174), and Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) achieved the strongest conversion rate among major case types at 66.1% (37 of 56 heard).
